social.title: An Evening in Patio Bellavista
social.description: An enclosed courtyard block at the foot of Cerro San Cristóbal packed with bars, terraces and craft stalls — the easiest possible first night out in Santiago.
social.bonus: Start with a pisco sour on an upstairs terrace.

social.title: Pisco Flight at Chipe Libre
social.description: The self-declared Independent Republic of Pisco on Lastarria, pouring Chilean and Peruvian pisco side by side and letting you settle the argument yourself.
social.bonus: Take the comparative flight and pick a side out loud.

social.title: Late Night at Blondie
social.description: A multi-floor club on the Alameda running since the early nineties, with a different decade of music on every level and nothing happening before one in the morning.
social.bonus: Find the floor playing the worst music and stay there.

social.title: See a Band at Teatro Caupolicán
social.description: A 1930s downtown theatre that became the city's great rock room — steep balconies, terrible sightlines from the back, and a crowd that sings over the band.
social.bonus: Get down into the stalls rather than sitting upstairs.

social.title: Match Day at the Estadio Nacional
social.description: Universidad de Chile at the national stadium — flares, full-stadium songs and a level of noise that makes conversation pointless for ninety minutes.
social.bonus: Buy a completo from a street cart outside before you go in.

social.title: Learn to Dance Salsa at Maestra Vida
social.description: A long-running Bellavista salsa club that runs a beginners' class early and then hands the floor over to people who have been dancing there for twenty years.
social.bonus: Stay for the live band and ask someone who can actually dance.

social.title: Bar-Hop the Corners of Barrio Brasil
social.description: Faded mansions around Plaza Brasil turned into cheap student bars and schoperias — loud, unpolished, and where the city actually drinks midweek.
social.bonus: Order a litre of schop and share it, as intended.

social.title: Cumbia Night at El Huaso Enrique
social.description: A Barrio Yungay dance hall open since 1943, with a live cumbia band, plastic tablecloths and couples of every age on the floor from the first song.
social.bonus: Do not sit down. Nobody else will let you.

social.title: Colo-Colo Match at Estadio Monumental
social.description: Feel the whole stadium sing when Colo-Colo takes the pitch at their fortress in Macul.

social.title: Bar-Hop Barrio Lastarria
social.description: Work your way through Lastarria's cobblestone bars and courtyard cafés with no plan beyond the next open door.
social.bonus: Talk to someone at the bar you don't know

social.title: Live Folk Music at La Casa en el Aire
social.description: Catch a live folk band at this Bellavista institution and let the cueca dancers pull you onto the floor.
social.bonus: Ask someone to teach you a cueca step

social.title: Lomito and People-Watching at Fuente Alemana
social.description: Grab a stool at the counter of this downtown institution for a towering lomito sandwich and prime people-watching.
social.bonus: Order it 'completo' with everything on it

culture.title: The Pre-Columbian Museum's Chinchorro Mummies
culture.description: The best museum in Chile, holding Chinchorro mummies that predate the Egyptian ones by two thousand years, plus Andean textiles and Mapuche silverwork.
culture.bonus: Go down to the basement gallery first, before the crowds.

culture.title: Twentieth-Century Clothes at the Museo de la Moda
culture.description: A modernist Vitacura house holding one of the world's great private fashion collections — including garments worn by Lady Diana, Marilyn Monroe and John Lennon.
culture.bonus: The house itself is the exhibit. Look at the architecture too.

culture.title: Contemporary Chilean Art at MAVI
culture.description: A quiet concrete-and-glass museum tucked behind Plaza Mulato Gil in Lastarria, showing living Chilean artists rather than the canon.
culture.bonus: Have a coffee in the plaza courtyard afterwards and watch the buskers.

culture.title: Walk the Cementerio General
culture.description: Two million graves laid out in avenues — presidents, Victor Jara, and the memorial to the disappeared — a walk through the whole of modern Chilean history.
culture.bonus: Find Salvador Allende's tomb and read what is written on it.

culture.title: Chilean Painting at the Museo de Bellas Artes
culture.description: A glass-domed Beaux-Arts palace built for the 1910 centenary, holding the national collection of Chilean painting and sculpture under one enormous skylight.
culture.bonus: Stand directly under the centre of the dome and look up.

culture.title: Fiestas Patrias in a Fonda
culture.description: Every September the country stops and builds fondas — temporary halls of cueca dancing, anticuchos, terremoto jugs and rodeo — the biggest in Parque O'Higgins.
culture.bonus: Learn the cueca handkerchief step before you go.

culture.title: A Night at the Teatro Municipal
culture.description: Chile's opera house since 1857, all red velvet and gold leaf, home to the national ballet and an opera season that fills every tier.
culture.bonus: Cheap upper-gallery seats have the best acoustics in the house.

culture.title: La Moneda and the Palace Beneath It
culture.description: The presidential palace bombed in the 1973 coup, with a cultural centre dug in underneath it showing major exhibitions in what were once the cellars.
culture.bonus: Time it for the changing of the guard in the Plaza de la Constitución.

chill.title: Soak in the Hot Springs at Valle de Colina
chill.description: Terraced thermal pools stacked up a mountainside at the far end of the Cajón del Maipo, each one a different temperature, with snow peaks on every side.
chill.bonus: Work your way down from the hottest pool to the coldest.

chill.title: Read the Afternoon Away in Parque Forestal
chill.description: A long ribbon of plane trees along the Mapocho, with the Beaux-Arts palace of the fine arts museum at its centre and students spread across the lawns all afternoon.
chill.bonus: Buy a mote con huesillo from a cart and drink it on the grass.

chill.title: Sunset on the Lawns of Parque Araucano
chill.description: Thirty hectares of open lawn and rose garden in Las Condes where the cordillera turns pink at dusk and the whole neighbourhood comes out to watch it.
chill.bonus: Stay until the mountains lose their colour completely.

chill.title: A Slow Sunday in Quinta Normal
chill.description: A 19th-century botanical park in the west of the city with a boating lake, enormous old trees and families out in force every Sunday afternoon.
chill.bonus: Take a rowboat out on the lagoon for half an hour.

chill.title: Climb the Terraces of Cerro Santa Lucía
chill.description: The rocky outcrop where Santiago was founded in 1541, landscaped into a maze of stone stairways, fountains and neoclassical terraces in the middle of downtown.
chill.bonus: Find the Neptune fountain, then keep climbing to the very top.

chill.title: Wander the Faded Streets of Barrio Yungay
chill.description: The city's first designated heritage neighbourhood — crumbling 19th-century facades, muralled walls, and the Peluquería Francesa barbershop unchanged since 1868.
chill.bonus: Get a coffee at the Peluquería Francesa and look up at the ceiling.

chill.title: Sunset from Sky Costanera
chill.description: Ride the express elevator to South America's highest viewpoint and watch the Andes turn pink over the city.
chill.bonus: Try to spot your own neighborhood from the deck

chill.title: Wander Bellavista and Tour La Chascona
chill.description: Stroll the bohemian streets of Bellavista and tour Pablo Neruda's whimsical hillside house-turned-museum.
chill.bonus: Write a line in the guestbook

chill.title: Afternoon at the Museum of Memory and Human Rights
chill.description: Move slowly through this striking museum's account of Chile's recent history — quiet, powerful, worth the full visit.
chill.bonus: Read one testimony all the way through

chill.title: Picnic at Parque Bicentenario
chill.description: Spread a blanket by the lagoon in Vitacura's manicured park and watch the resident flamingos while the city hums around you.
chill.bonus: Bring bread for the ducks by the pond

8ball.title: Get Off at a Metro Station You've Never Used
8ball.description: Santiago has one of the best metros in the Americas and you probably use six stations of it. Ride to one you have never stood in, surface, and eat at the first place with a queue.
8ball.bonus: No maps and no reviews until after you have ordered.

8ball.title: Head East Until the Cordillera Fills the Windscreen
8ball.description: Pick any road heading east out of the city and follow it until the Andes stop being scenery and start being the entire view. Then find somewhere to sit and look at them.
8ball.bonus: Go far enough that you lose phone signal.

foodie.title: Eat and Drink Your Way Down Barrio Italia
foodie.description: Old furniture workshops off Avenida Italia now hold courtyard restaurants, coffee roasters and wine bars behind unmarked doors — wander until something looks right.
foodie.bonus: Go through an archway that has no sign on it.

foodie.title: Pastel de Choclo at Galindo
foodie.description: A loud, unfussy Bellavista picada that has been serving the same Chilean home cooking for decades — pastel de choclo in a clay dish, straight out of the oven.
foodie.bonus: Order a schop and let it come in whatever glass arrives.

foodie.title: The Endemic Tasting Menu at Boragó
foodie.description: Rodolfo Guzmán cooks only what grows wild in Chile — Patagonian seaweed, Atacama herbs, ants from the south — across a twenty-course menu found nowhere else on earth.
foodie.bonus: Ask which ingredient travelled furthest to reach your plate.

foodie.title: Empanadas at Emporio Zunino
foodie.description: A counter beside the Mercado Central turning out empanadas de pino since 1930 — no seats, no menu beyond what is in the tray, and a queue out the door at noon.
foodie.bonus: Eat it standing on the pavement like everyone else.

foodie.title: A Sandwich at Confitería Torres
foodie.description: Open on the Alameda since 1879, with red leather booths, waiters in waistcoats, and the barros luco sandwich reputedly invented here for a president.
foodie.bonus: Order the barros luco. It is named after the man who ate it daily.

foodie.title: Dinner at 99 Restaurante
foodie.description: A small Providencia dining room where the menu changes with whatever the market and the coast delivered that morning, at a fraction of what the cooking is worth.
foodie.bonus: Take the shorter menu and add a glass pairing.

foodie.title: Tour the Cellars at Concha y Toro
foodie.description: Forty minutes south to Pirque, where the Casillero del Diablo cellar earned its name from a founder who spread a devil rumour to stop staff stealing his wine.
foodie.bonus: Do the tasting in the dark cellar, not the terrace.

foodie.title: Wine and Andean Artefacts at Santa Rita
foodie.description: A 19th-century estate at Alto Jahuel with a colonial-era cellar, a long lunch under century-old trees, and a pre-Columbian museum in the grounds.
foodie.bonus: Walk the park before lunch, not after.

foodie.title: Seafood Lunch at Mercado Central
foodie.description: Pull up a stool inside the iron-and-glass market hall and order whatever's freshest off the boat that morning.
foodie.bonus: Let the vendor pick your fish for you

foodie.title: Pisco Sours at La Piojera
foodie.description: Squeeze into Santiago's rowdiest century-old dive bar for a pisco sour poured the old-fashioned way.
foodie.bonus: Order a terremoto and split it

foodie.title: Chilean Wine Flight at Bocanáriz
foodie.description: Settle into Barrio Lastarria's best wine bar for a curated flight spanning Chile's valleys from Casablanca to Colchagua.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier for a varietal you've never heard of

foodie.title: Market Crawl Through La Vega Central
foodie.description: Get lost in the stalls of Chile's biggest produce market and snack your way from empanada carts to fresh juice stands.
foodie.bonus: Buy a fruit you've never tried before

adventure.title: Spend a Day in Valparaíso
adventure.description: Ninety minutes by bus to a port city built up forty-two hills — Victorian funiculars, murals on every wall, and Neruda's house at La Sebastiana on the way down.
adventure.bonus: Ride at least three different ascensores.

adventure.title: Summit Cerro Provincia in a Single Day
adventure.description: Eighteen hundred metres of ascent from the Puente Ñilhue trailhead to a 2,750-metre summit — the classic Santiago day mountain, and a genuinely hard one.
adventure.bonus: Carry four litres of water. There is none on the route.

adventure.title: Sunrise Scramble Up Cerro Pochoco
adventure.description: A steep, straightforward hour and a half above Lo Barnechea to an old observatory, with the whole basin laid out beneath you before the smog settles.
adventure.bonus: Be on the summit before the sun clears the cordillera.

adventure.title: Ride the Mapocho 42K End to End
adventure.description: A continuous riverside bike path running forty-two kilometres along the Mapocho, from the wealthy foothills right through to the working-class west.
adventure.bonus: Ride it downstream and take the Metro home.

adventure.title: Drive to the Turquoise Water of Embalse El Yeso
adventure.description: A glacial reservoir high in the Cajón del Maipo, unreasonably turquoise and ringed by 4,000-metre peaks, at the end of a rough dirt road two hours from the city.
adventure.bonus: Wade in up to your knees. You will not last longer.

adventure.title: Hike to the Salto de Apoquindo Waterfall
adventure.description: A long climb up Parque Aguas de Ramón through cactus and litre trees to a fifty-metre waterfall falling off the Andean front range, all inside the city limits.
adventure.bonus: Get to the trailhead by eight — the park closes its gate early.

adventure.title: Walk the Palm Forest of La Campana
adventure.description: The last great stand of Chilean wine palms, in the national park Darwin climbed in 1834 and wrote up in the Beagle diaries.
adventure.bonus: Read Darwin's entry on the summit before you start down.

adventure.title: Learn to Surf at Matanzas
adventure.description: A wind-battered fishing village two hours southwest that became Chile's kitesurf and surf capital — board hire, wetsuits and lessons right on the sand.
adventure.bonus: Stay for the empanadas at the top of the hill afterwards.

adventure.title: City Bike Tour with La Bicicleta Verde
adventure.description: Pedal through Santiago's parks, plazas, and street art with a local guide narrating the city's history along the way.
adventure.bonus: Wave back at every dog you pass

adventure.title: Whitewater Rafting the Río Maipo
adventure.description: Paddle Class III–IV rapids on the Río Maipo with a guided crew before regrouping for lunch streamside.
adventure.bonus: Call out to take the front row of the raft

adventure.title: Canopy Zipline at Cascada de las Ánimas
adventure.description: Fly across the Cajón del Maipo canyon on a string of ziplines strung above the Río Maipo.
adventure.bonus: Keep your eyes open the whole way across the longest line

adventure.title: Ski Day at Valle Nevado
adventure.description: Carve fresh Andean powder an hour from the city at one of South America's best ski resorts.
adventure.bonus: Try a run above your usual level

adventure.title: Glacier Hike to El Morado and Hot Springs at Baños Morales
adventure.description: Trek through Cajón del Maipo to the glacial lake at El Morado, then ease into the hot springs at Baños Morales on the way home.
adventure.bonus: Soak until your legs actually stop aching

adventure.title: Sunrise Hike Up Cerro San Cristóbal
adventure.description: Climb the switchback trail through Parque Metropolitano to the summit and watch the Andes catch first light over the city.
adventure.bonus: Take the funicular down instead of walking
